events_on_republican.what: Augustus set up the obelisk of Ramesses II on the spina; the pulvinar was added (Pliny NH 36.71; Res Gestae 'obelisk in Circus' # unverified; Suet. Aug. 45)
fire on the Aventine side destroyed part (Tac. Ann. 6.45)
Claudius rebuilt the starting gates in tufa and the turning-posts gilded (Suet. Claud. 21)
fire began in the shops on the Palatine/Aventine side of the circus and spread (Tac. Ann. 15.38); Nero later rebuilt (Suet. Nero 38)
Domitian restored the circus (Suet. Dom. 5); passage unverified
burned 19 December AD 69 in the fight between Flavian and Vitellian troops (Tac. Hist. 3.71-72)
foundation of the new temple laid 21 June AD 70 with the haruspices' rites (Tac. Hist. 4.53); dedicated by Vespasian c. AD 75
burned again in AD 80 (Suet. Titus 8; Dio 66.24.2)
rebuilt by Domitian, with gilded roof (Suet. Dom. 5; Plut. Publ. 15)
Rostra Iulia added in front of the temple of Divus Julius (Dio 51.19.2)
rebuilt by Tiberius and dedicated AD 6 (Suet. Tib. 20; Dio 55.27.4)
rebuilt by Tiberius and dedicated AD 10 (Suet. Tib. 20; Dio 56.25.1)
stage burned and restored by Tiberius (Tac. Ann. 3.72; Dio 57.21.3)
burned in AD 80, restored by Domitian (Dio 66.24.2)
burned in the fire of AD 64 (Tac. Ann. 15.41)

built.by: Augustus; vowed at Philippi 42 BC, forum opened 2 BC with games (Suet. Aug. 29; Res Gestae 21; Dio 55.10.1-8)

events.what: dedicated 1 August 2 BC with the temple of Mars Ultor; statues of the summi viri in the porticoes with elogia (Suet. Aug. 31, 29; Ovid Fasti 5.545-598)

monuments.form: colonnaded forum with two apsidal exedrae and a high firewall (travertine/peperino) at the rear against the Subura
monuments.location: Between the Forum of Caesar and the Subura wall, north-east of the Forum Romanum; partly under Via dei Fori Imperiali
monuments.notes: Size and bearing from memory of the plan (long axis NE-SW, temple at the NE end); unverified.

built.by: Augustus, vowed 42 BC at Philippi; dedicated 1 August 2 BC (Suet. Aug. 29; Dio 55.10.1-3; Res Gestae 21)

events.what: The standards recovered from the Parthians (20 BC) were placed in the temple (Dio 54.8.3; Res Gestae 29; Dio 55.10.3); the Senate was to vote triumphs there and generals to set out from it (Suet. Aug. 29)

monuments.form: octastyle Corinthian temple, Luna marble, cult statues of Mars, Venus and Divus Julius
monuments.location: North-east end of the Forum of Augustus, backing on the Subura firewall
monuments.notes: Dimensions from memory (podium ~ 3.5 m high); unverified. Front faces south-west into the forum (bearing_deg is the direction the front faces).

built.by: Augustus; vowed 36 BC after Naulochus, dedicated 9 October 28 BC (Res Gestae 19; Suet. Aug. 29; Dio 53.1.3; Vell. 2.81)

monuments.english: Temple of Apollo on the Palatine

events.what: dedication with library (Greek and Latin) in the adjoining porticus with statues of the Danaids (Suet. Aug. 29; Prop. 2.31)

monuments.form: temple of Luna marble with quadriga on the roof, doors of ivory; porticus with 50 columns of African marble (Prop. 2.31)
monuments.location: Palatine, next to Augustus' house; its identification with the podium by the Casa di Livia / the 'Area Apollinis' is debated
monuments.notes: Site contested (Carettoni's 1960s excavation near the Casa di Livia vs. other candidates).

built.by: Augustus in his sixth consulship, 28 BC (Suet. Aug. 100; Strabo 5.3.8)

events.what: Marcellus first to be buried there (Dio 53.30.5)
Augustus' ashes deposited; Res Gestae set up on bronze pillars in front (Suet. Aug. 101; Res Gestae preface)

monuments.form: tumulus on a travertine drum, concentric walls, topped by a colossal bronze statue of Augustus; two obelisks at the entrance (now Quirinal and Esquiline)
monuments.location: Campus Martius, between the Via Flaminia and the Tiber, Piazza Augusto Imperatore
monuments.notes: Diameter ~87 m and height ~42 m from memory of modern reconstructions (height is conjectural).

built.by: Senate decree 13 BC on Augustus' return from Spain and Gaul; dedicated 30 January 9 BC (Res Gestae 12; Ovid Fasti 1.709-722)

monuments.form: marble precinct wall with altar inside, relief procession; sacrificial altar on a raised base
monuments.location: Campus Martius, west of the Via Flaminia (Via Lata); original site under Palazzo Fiano, now re-erected beside the Mausoleum
monuments.notes: Size (11.65 x 10.62 x ~3.7 m) from memory of the reconstruction; the main entrance faces west, the altar is inside at the east - axis taken as E-W; unverified.

built.by: Augustus; obelisk of Psammetichus II brought from Heliopolis and set up in the Campus Martius as a gnomon, 10 BC (Pliny NH 36.71-73; the dedication to the Sun on the base is quoted in CIL VI 701 - not re-read)

monuments.english: Sundial (Horologium) of Augustus and its obelisk
monuments.form: obelisk about 21.8 m high on a bronze-lettered meridian, with a pavement of bronze lines and Greek letters
monuments.location: Campus Martius, around Piazza di Montecitorio and Via del Campo Marzio; the obelisk now stands in Piazza di Montecitorio
monuments.notes: Whether the meridian really worked as a sundial (Buchner 1982) vs. a monument alone is contested; the 160 x 75 m size and the Ara Pacis alignment are Buchner's reconstruction - unverified. Pliny NH 36.72-73 also remarks that the gnomon had ceased to mark the hours accurately in his own day; unverified detail.

built.by: M. Agrippa as consul 27 BC, dedicated c. 25 BC (Dio 53.27.2; Pliny NH 36.38; Pliny 34.13 on caryatids)

events.what: burned in the fire of AD 80 (Dio 66.24.2)
later tradition (Jerome/Orosius, not read) reports a lightning fire under Trajan; rebuilding is then attributed to Domitian after 80 and to Hadrian (see pantheon_hadriani) - unverified

monuments.form: rectangular temple facing south (excavation evidence) with a pronaos, ~ 43 x 20 m; Caryatids (Pliny 36.38) by Diogenes of Athens in the interior
monuments.location: Campus Martius, Piazza della Rotonda; Hadrian's rotunda stands on the same site
monuments.notes: Agrippa's building was not the rotunda; its plan comes from Ziolkowski/Hetland's excavations of the 1890s and 1990s. Date of the AD 110 fire from Orosius/Jerome; unverified. Dimensions from memory.

built.by: Hadrian, c. AD 118-128; brick stamps of 123-125 date the rotunda; the inscription copies Agrippa's (HA Hadr. 19.10; Dio 69.7)

monuments.form: rotunda 43.3 m in diameter and height under a coffered concrete dome with an oculus 8.9 m wide; portico of 16 granite Corinthian columns (8 across the front) at 34 m wide
monuments.location: Campus Martius, Piazza della Rotonda
monuments.notes: Just beyond the 27 BC - AD 120 window if the rebuilding is placed c. 125; kept because the task asked for it. Front faces roughly north; exact bearing not recorded here (set 0 for placement only).

built.by: M. Agrippa; baths 25 BC with the Euripus channel (Dio 53.27.1; Pliny NH 36.121); bequeathed to the Roman people in his will 12 BC (Dio 54.29.4)

events.what: bequeathed with the gardens to the people free of charge (Dio 54.29.4)
damaged in the fire of AD 80 and restored (Dio 66.24.2)

monuments.form: first imperial bath complex in Rome, with a stagnum and Euripus; Lysippus's Apoxyomenos stood before them (Pliny NH 34.62)
monuments.location: Campus Martius, between the Pantheon and the Saepta; the Stagnum Agrippae to the south-west
monuments.notes: Footprint approximate from memory; the 80 AD restoration entry unverified.

built.by: begun by Julius Caesar, continued by Lepidus, dedicated by Agrippa 26 BC (Dio 53.23.1-2; Cic. Att. 4.16.8)

events.what: burned in AD 80, restored by Domitian (Dio 66.24.2; Mart. 9.59 for the shops)

monuments.form: vast rectangular marble portico enclosure with voting pens, later a shopping and exhibition place
monuments.location: Campus Martius, east of the Pantheon, along the Via Lata, between Piazza del Collegio Romano and the Pantheon
monuments.notes: Size from memory (Forma Urbis fragments); the restorations in AD 80 and by Domitian unverified.

built.by: begun by Caesar, completed by Augustus and named for his nephew Marcellus (Suet. Aug. 29; Dio 43.49.2, 54.26.1; Res Gestae 21)

events.what: dedicated 13 or 11 BC (Dio 54.26.1 says 13 BC; Pliny NH 8.65 describes tigers at the dedication in 11 BC); reconstructed also after AD 64 (unverified)

monuments.form: tiered semicircular theatre, arcade outer wall of 41 arches in two orders (Doric, Ionic) over concrete radial vaults; later a third attic level
monuments.location: Between the Capitol and the Tiber, Forum Holitorium side; the arcaded outer wall still stands in Via del Teatro di Marcello
monuments.notes: Dedication year: 13 BC (Dio) vs 11 BC (Pliny/others); scholars differ.

built.by: L. Cornelius Balbus, dedicated 13 BC (Suet. Aug. 29; Dio 54.25.2; Pliny NH 36.60)

events.what: burned in AD 80 and restored by Titus (Suet. Dio 66.24.2) - unverified

monuments.form: theatre with a Crypta (covered portico) behind it; capacity 6,000 or 11,600 in the late Regionary lists
monuments.location: Campus Martius, near the Circus Flaminius; Crypta Balbi on Via delle Botteghe Oscure marks the portico
monuments.notes: Radius is a guess from the cavea curve in Via delle Botteghe Oscure; the AD 80 restoration line is unverified.

built.by: Augustus rebuilt the Porticus Metelli of 146 BC in the name of his sister Octavia, after 33 BC; Suet. Aug. 29; Dio 49.43.8; Pliny NH 34.31

events.what: burned in AD 80 (Dio 66.24.2); restored later by Septimius Severus (outside range)

monuments.form: rectangular double portico enclosing the temples of Juno and Jupiter Stator, with a library and the Curia Octaviae
monuments.location: Between the Theatre of Marcellus and the Circus Flaminius; the propylaeum survives at the church of S. Angelo in Pescheria
monuments.notes: Size from memory of the Forma Urbis plan (~ 119 x 132 m), unverified.

built.by: triumvirs/Octavian; dedicated 18 August 29 BC (Dio 47.18.4, 51.22.1)

events.what: Rostra Iulia at its front, decorated with the rostra of Actium (Dio 51.19.2)

monuments.form: Ionic hexastyle temple on a high podium with a rostra platform in front
monuments.location: East end of the Forum Romanum, on the site of Caesar's pyre
monuments.notes: Dimensions and bearing (front faces west into the Forum) from memory; unverified.

built.by: begun by Caesar; completed and dedicated by Octavian 29 BC (Dio 51.22.1; Res Gestae 19)

events.what: burned in the fire of AD 64 (Tac. Ann. 15.38-44 for the general fire) - this specific loss is not read
burned in AD 80 and rebuilt by Domitian (Dio 66.24.2; Suet. Dom. 5 for the Domitianic rebuildings)

monuments.form: rectangular hall with three tiers of senators' benches along each side; Altar and Statue of Victory inside (Dio 51.22.1)
monuments.location: North side of the Forum Romanum, next to the Comitium
monuments.notes: The standing building is Diocletian's; the Augustan plan is inferred from it; 21 x 27 m is the standing size. AD 64 line unverified.

built.by: begun by Caesar (dedicated unfinished 46 BC), completed by Augustus after a fire, dedicated in the names of Gaius and Lucius (Suet. Aug. 29; Res Gestae 20)

events.what: second rebuilding after a fire; rededicated (Res Gestae 20 and Suet. Aug. 29 speak of Augustus completing it after fire; the specific second-dedication year is not read) - unverified

monuments.form: basilica with a central hall and double aisles, centumviral court seat
monuments.location: South side of the Forum Romanum between the Temples of Saturn and Castor
monuments.notes: 101 x 49 m is the modern-excavation figure from memory. Dedication year(s) after the fire unverified.

built.by: Agrippa as aedile 33 BC, repairing the Marcia and Tepula and adding the new Julia (Frontin. Aq. 9; Dio 49.42.1)

monuments.form: channel above the Tepula in the same arches as the Marcia and Tepula
monuments.location: Springs near the 6th mile of the Via Latina; runs on the Marcia/Tepula channel to Rome
monuments.notes: Route is a straight-line schematic, rough. Duplicates the Republican-file entry for the Julia because the Republic file covers it to 27 BC.

built.by: Agrippa 19 BC (Frontin. Aq. 10; Dio 54.11.7)

events.what: repaired by Claudius (Frontin. Aq. 10) - unverified

monuments.form: about 14,105 paces long, mostly underground, only about 1,200 paces on arches (Frontin. Aq. 10)
monuments.location: Springs at the 8th mile of the Via Collatina; the channel enters Rome beneath the Pincian, then flows in Campus Martius
monuments.notes: Route schematic and rough; the Claudian restoration (Frontinus puts Claudius' repairs at Aq. 10) is read from memory only.

built.by: Augustus, to feed his Naumachia in Trastevere (Frontin. Aq. 11)

monuments.form: about 22,172 paces long, poor water, not for drinking (Frontin. Aq. 11)
monuments.location: From Lake Alsietinus (Martignano), ending in Trastevere on the Janiculum
monuments.notes: Date 2 BC from the naumachia, not read.

built.by: Tiberius (Suet. Tib. 15 # unverified), enlarged by Caligula and Nero (Suet. Cal. 22 on the bridge to the Capitol)

events.what: burned in the fire of AD 64 (Tac. Ann. 15.39 for the Palatine) - unverified for this palace

monuments.form: large palace complex of concrete vaults round a central court; the greater part later covered by the Farnese gardens
monuments.location: North-west corner of the Palatine, above the Forum and the Clivus Victoriae
monuments.notes: Size from memory; the date of the earliest phase is debated (it may be Tiberian only in name; the visible plan is largely Flavian-Hadrianic).

built.by: Tiberius at the urging of Sejanus (Tac. Ann. 4.2; Suet. Tib. 37; Dio 57.19.6)

monuments.form: rectangular fort with brick walls and corner towers; the later wall height raised under Aurelian
monuments.location: North-east of the city on the Viminal/Quirinal edge, beside the Servian wall; the brick walls survive
monuments.notes: Size from memory (about 440 x 380 m); the walls are roughly aligned with the cardinal directions, set 0.

built.by: begun by Tiberius, completed and dedicated by Caligula (Suet. Cal. 21; Tac. Ann. 6.45; Dio 59.7.1)

events.what: burned in AD 80 and rebuilt by Domitian (Dio 66.24.2; Suet. Dom. 5) - unverified for this temple

monuments.form: temple; Caligula also built a bridge between this temple and the Capitol (Suet. Cal. 22)
monuments.location: Possibly near the Forum, between the Vicus Tuscus and the Palatine; the site (S. Maria Antiqua area, a modern hypothesis) is not agreed
monuments.notes: Site very doubtful; position is a placeholder.

built.by: T. Statilius Taurus, with Augustus' backing (Dio 51.23.1; Suet. Aug. 29)

events.what: destroyed in the fire of AD 64 (Dio 62.18.2) - unverified

monuments.form: first stone amphitheatre in Rome, partly timber
monuments.location: Campus Martius, exact site lost
monuments.notes: Position placeholder; AD 64 entry unverified.

built.by: Augustus, fed by the Aqua Alsietina; sea-fight of Athenians vs Persians staged there (Res Gestae 23; Dio 55.10.7)

monuments.form: artificial lake about 1,800 x 1,200 Roman feet (Res Gestae 23)
monuments.location: Trastevere, across the Tiber, beside the grove of the Caesars (Nemus Caesarum)
monuments.notes: Size converted (1,800 x 1,200 feet at 0.296 m); location rough.

built.by: begun by Gaius AD 38, finished and dedicated by Claudius 1 August AD 52 (Frontin. Aq. 13-14; Suet. Claud. 20; Pliny NH 36.122)

monuments.form: about 46,406 paces, of which about 9,500 on arches; the monument at Porta Maggiore carries the Claudia and Anio Novus channels one above the other (Frontin. Aq. 13)
monuments.location: Springs at the 38th mile of the Via Sublacensis; enters Rome at the Porta Maggiore (Porta Praenestina) on high arches
monuments.notes: Route schematic; lengths from memory of Frontinus, unverified.

built.by: begun by Gaius AD 38, dedicated by Claudius 1 August AD 52 (Frontin. Aq. 15; Suet. Claud. 20)

monuments.form: about 58,700 paces, the highest-level aqueduct of Rome (Frontin. Aq. 15)
monuments.location: Anio valley above Subiaco, entering Rome at the Porta Maggiore on the upper channel of the Claudia arches
monuments.notes: Length from memory; the prompt text said 'Claudia and Anio Novus (AD 52)'. Route schematic.

built.by: Senate for Claudius' conquest of Britain, AD 51-52 (CIL VI 920; Dio 60.22)

monuments.english: Arch of Claudius on the Via Lata
monuments.form: arch carrying the Aqua Virgo over the Via Lata; inscription survives (CIL 6.920)
monuments.location: Via Lata (Corso), where the Aqua Virgo crossed it; site approximate
monuments.notes: Position placeholder.

built.by: Nero; destroyed by the fire of AD 64 (Suet. Nero 31; Tac. Ann. 15.39)

events.what: burned in the fire, though Nero's house was said to have been reached by the flames (Tac. Ann. 15.39)

monuments.form: palace linking the Palatine and the Esquiline (the 'Transitoria' name from this passage)
monuments.location: Palatine joined to the Esquiline gardens of Maecenas; remains below the Domus Flavia and under the Palatine
monuments.notes: Rough site. The start date 60 is a guess from the Neronian buildings; unverified.

built.by: Fire of 18-19 July AD 64; six days and seven nights; of the 14 regions four remained whole, three were levelled, seven left with few traces (Tac. Ann. 15.38-41; Suet. Nero 38; Dio 62.16-18)

events.what: Nero rebuilt with a stricter building code (Tac. Ann. 15.43)

monuments.form: city fire
monuments.location: Began in the shops by the Circus Maximus (Tac. Ann. 15.38); swept the Palatine, Velabrum, Forum and Caelian
monuments.notes: Not a building; kept as a map overlay entry. Tacitus gives night of 18/19 July; passages not re-read.

built.by: Nero after the fire, architects Severus and Celer (Tac. Ann. 15.42; Suet. Nero 31)

events.what: unfinished at Nero's death
Vespasian gave the lake area to the people for the amphitheatre (Suet. Vesp. 9; Martial Spect. 2)

monuments.form: vestibule with a colossal statue 120 feet high, a lake 'like a sea' surrounded by buildings, ivory-ceilinged dining rooms, revolving dome (Suet. Nero 31)
monuments.location: Oppian hill (surviving wing under the Baths of Trajan); the park occupied the valley between Palatine, Caelian and Esquiline
monuments.notes: Footprint is a vague estimate (the park claimed an immense area, Suet. Nero 31); the surviving wing is the Oppian one.

built.by: Nero, by Zenodorus; 106.5 feet (Pliny NH 34.45); 120 feet (Suet. Nero 31)

events.what: Vespasian turned it into the Sun with a radiate crown (Suet. Vesp. 18; Pliny NH 34.45); Hadrian moved it with 24 elephants (HA Hadr. 19.12) - beyond range

monuments.form: bronze colossus, a standing statue about 30-35 m high
monuments.location: Vestibule of the Domus Aurea on the Velia; base later beside the Temple of Venus and Roma, near the Colosseum
monuments.notes: Pliny and Suetonius differ on the height (106.5 vs 120 Roman feet); base position from memory.

built.by: Nero (coin sestertii c. 64; Dio 61.18.3)

monuments.form: circular central colonnade on the Caelian
monuments.location: Caelian hill
monuments.notes: Dio 61.18.3 reference and date from memory; unverified.

built.by: Nero, dedicated AD 60 (gymnasium) and 62 (baths) (Tac. Ann. 14.47, 15.22; Suet. Nero 12; Dio 62.21)

monuments.form: large hot baths; renowned (Martial 7.34; Juv. 7.233) - unverified
monuments.location: Campus Martius, between the Pantheon and the Stadium of Domitian (S. Luigi dei Francesi / Piazza Navona area)
monuments.notes: Gymnasium AD 60 / baths AD 62 - dates not re-read. Site rough.

built.by: begun by Agrippina after Claudius' deification, largely demolished by Nero, completed by Vespasian (Suet. Vesp. 9)

monuments.form: temple on an immense terraced platform with a nymphaeum on the Via Triumphalis side
monuments.location: Caelian hill, on the platform under S. Stefano Rotondo and the Passionist monastery of SS. Giovanni e Paolo
monuments.notes: Footprint is the platform from memory (about 180 x 200 m); unverified.

built.by: begun by Vespasian c. AD 70-72 on the site of Nero's lake (Suet. Vesp. 9; Martial Spect. 2), dedicated by Titus in AD 80 with 100 days of games (Suet. Titus 7; Dio 66.25), top storeys finished by Domitian (Suet. Dom. 5)

events.what: inaugural games, 100 days; 9,000 wild animals killed (Dio 66.25)
struck by lightning (beyond range)

monuments.form: elliptical amphitheatre of four storeys, arena 83 x 48 m, outer wall 188 x 156 m, height ~ 48 m, seating for about 50,000
monuments.location: In the drained lake of Nero's Domus Aurea, between the Velia, Caelian and Oppian
monuments.notes: Dimensions are those given in the task (Platner-Ashby s.v.), not re-read. Long-axis bearing from memory of the map and unverified. 'Begun c. AD 70-72' is the task's figure.

built.by: Domitian (Regionary catalogues and brick stamps); the Hadrianic/Trajanic form is later

monuments.form: elliptical training arena with seating for about 3,000 inside a rectangular barracks courtyard
monuments.location: East of the Colosseum between the Caelian and the Oppian, connected by passage to the amphitheatre
monuments.notes: Domitianic date inferred from memory; unverified.

built.by: Titus (Suet. Titus 7; Martial Spect. 2; Dio 66.25)

monuments.form: small bath complex built quickly in AD 80, later swallowed by the Baths of Trajan
monuments.location: Oppian hill on part of the Domus Aurea, near the Colosseum
monuments.notes: Footprint a guess; unverified.

built.by: Senate and People after Titus' death and deification (CIL VI 945); relief of the Jewish triumph of AD 71; erected c. AD 81 under Domitian

monuments.form: single-bay arch of Pentelic marble, relief panels of the triumph with the Temple's menorah
monuments.location: Summa Sacra Via, on the Velia ridge east of the Forum Romanum
monuments.notes: Dimensions from memory; whether it was built under Titus or Domitian is the usual debate; the inscription names the deified Titus.

built.by: begun by Titus, completed by Domitian after AD 87 (Suet. Dom. 5; Platner-Ashby)

monuments.form: hexastyle Corinthian temple on a high podium, 7.6 m shaft
monuments.location: Foot of the Capitol, between the Temple of Saturn and the Tabularium; three Corinthian columns stand
monuments.notes: Year from memory (~ AD 87-91); unverified.

built.by: Vespasian, dedicated AD 75 (Dio 66.15.1; Josephus BJ 7.158-162)

events.what: burned in AD 192 (beyond range)

monuments.form: rectangular garden court with porticoes on three sides and a temple to Pax on the south-east; held the treasures of the Jewish war (Josephus BJ 7.158-162)
monuments.location: South-east of the Forum of Augustus, between the Via Sacra and the Argiletum; the Forma Urbis marble plan hung in an apse
monuments.notes: Size from memory; Pliny NH 36.102 praises it as among the most beautiful buildings (unread).

built.by: Domitian, architect Rabirius (Martial 7.56, 8.36; Stat. Silv. 4.2)

monuments.form: official half: peristyle court, triclinium (coenatio Iovis), basilica and aula regia
monuments.location: Central Palatine, over the earlier Neronian structures
monuments.notes: Date 'AD 92' from the Statius poem; the Domus Flavia/Augustana division is modern.

built.by: Domitian, architect Rabirius (Martial 7.56)

monuments.english: Domus Augustana (private wing of Domitian's palace)
monuments.form: private wing on two floors around a large peristyle with an elaborate island pool
monuments.location: South-east Palatine, over the Circus Maximus side; two-storey peristyle with a pool in maze form
monuments.notes: Footprint a guess; unverified.

built.by: Domitian (no source read; # unverified), later rebuilt by Theodoric

monuments.form: elongated garden court with portico, used as a private stadium
monuments.location: South-east of the Domus Augustana, Palatine
monuments.notes: Not the Stadium of Domitian in the Campus Martius.

built.by: Domitian, inaugurated with the Capitoline agon AD 86 (Suet. Dom. 4-5; Dio 67.8; Eus. Chron.)

monuments.form: athletic stadium, 30,000 seats, arcaded outer wall in travertine
monuments.location: Campus Martius, outline preserved by Piazza Navona
monuments.notes: Outline well known (Piazza Navona); capacity 30,000 and date AD 86 are from memory.

built.by: Domitian (Platner-Ashby s.v. Odeum; Suet. Dom. 5)

events.what: restored by Trajan, Apollodorus (Platner-Ashby)

monuments.form: covered concert hall, seating about 10,000
monuments.location: Campus Martius, west of the Stadium (Palazzo Massimo / Piazza dei Massimi area)
monuments.notes: Placement rough; the Trajanic restoration unverified.

built.by: begun by Domitian, completed and dedicated by Nerva AD 97 (Suet. Dom. 5; HA Alex. Sev. 28.6; Martial 1.2)

monuments.form: long narrow forum with a Temple of Minerva at one end; used as a passage between Subura and the Forum
monuments.location: Between the Forum of Augustus and the Temple of Peace, along the Argiletum; two columns 'Colonnacce' stand
monuments.notes: Dimensions from memory; unverified.

built.by: Titus/Domitian era (Platner-Ashby s.v. Meta Sudans)

monuments.form: conical brick-and-marble fountain, 17 m high
monuments.location: Between the Palatine and the Colosseum; base partially excavated
monuments.notes: Date is not secure; here as a compact landmark only.

built.by: Trajan, architect Apollodorus of Damascus (Dio 68.16; 69.4); forum dedicated AD 112, Basilica Ulpia and Column AD 113 (CIL VI 960)

monuments.form: forum with the equestrian statue of Trajan, the Basilica Ulpia, two libraries and the Column
monuments.location: Between the Capitol/Quirinal saddle and the Forum of Augustus; Via dei Fori Imperiali and the Column
monuments.notes: Overall size from memory incl. the exedrae and the Temple of Divus Traianus (added by Hadrian, beyond range).

built.by: Trajan; dedicated AD 112/113 (CIL VI 960)

monuments.form: basilica with five aisles, two apses, marble paving; height of nave 37 m
monuments.location: Northwest of the forum square of Trajan
monuments.notes: Dimensions from memory; unverified.

built.by: Senate and People, dedicated 12 May AD 113 (CIL VI 960)

monuments.form: Doric column with spiral relief frieze of the Dacian wars, 29.8 m high shaft; total height with base and pedestal about 35 m (100 Roman feet)
monuments.location: Between the Basilica Ulpia and the two libraries in the Forum of Trajan
monuments.notes: Height from memory.

built.by: Trajan, Apollodorus of Damascus; brick stamps date c. AD 110

monuments.form: multi-level semicircular range of shops and offices on the hillside
